reason: Both unplugged first, had the drum turned by hand and reached the same sensible 'engineer' endpoint without naming a definite part, so neither made unsupported claims. Conversation 2 gave a fuller, honest differential (jockey pulley/belt vs rollers/bearing), checked for trapped objects, attempted a sensible non-invasive localisation test, respected the customer's back-injury limitation gracefully, and set out clear stop-use triggers (constant squeal, drum catching, hot-rubber smell). Conversation 1 was efficient but thinner: it collected the model number only to say it couldn't match a part, offered no red-flag guidance, and leaned slightly harder on drum rollers without acknowledging the jockey pulley as the classic cold-start-squeal culprit. Neither asked about levelling or the condensate pump, so the gap is clear rather than decisive.
